paragraphs: Katab bechesed laalapim yesh lomar kol perate havvidduy "p sheen bo mehaddebarim hannizkarim bavvidduy, mippene dekol yisrael gup echad hem vekullam arebim zeh lazeh ubiprat im haya beyado limchot velo micha deniqra al shemo, ukemo shekkatebu rabbotenu za"l baggemara (shabbat nd:) al parato shel rabbi elazar ben azarya shehayeta yotzet birtzua shebben qarneha, shello shello hayeta ella shel shekento vehoil velo micha bah niqret al shemo, vegam od hu atzmo tzarik lehitvaddot al mah shechata baggilgulim sheaberu gam ken, umi yodea meh asa epshar sheabar al kol debarim ellu, velaken omerim nosach havvidduy chatanu anachnu vaabotenu, kelomar gilgulim haqqodemim shenniqraim abot lazeh haggup shehu od atta bo, veod name ikka tama baamirat kol havvidduy dehaadam niddon lepi mah shehu, dematzinu shekkatub biruben (bereshit lh, kb): vayyishkab im bilha baabur shebbilbel yetzue abiv, veal bene eli shakebu im hannashim (shemuel  b, kb) baabur sheshshahu qinnehen, ubene shemuel natu achare habbetza baabur dechelqam shaalu bepihem (shabbat nv.), veniktab al david hammelek alayv hashshalom aon bat sheba "p shehayeta megoreshet, vegam tabela minniddatah, vegam shahata shelosha chodashim dehabchana (sanhedrin qv-qz), veod name yesh aberot sheddash adam baaqebayv vachashuben lo kachamurot, kemo shemaro rabbotenu za"l hammalbin pene chabero keillu shopek damim (baba metzia nch-nt), vehakkoes keillu obed aboda zara (zohar ch" kz:), vehammitgaeh keillu obed obed zara (sota d-h) vekahenna rabbot, velaken mitztzad kol hatteamim haelleh tzarik haadam lomar kol perate havvidduy vekannizkar sham:

clarification.explanation: One should say all the details of the confession, even for things he did not do, for several reasons: (a) All of Israel are one body and all are guarantors for one another, and especially if it was in his power to protest his fellow's [wrongdoing] and he did not protest, this is also counted in his name (as with Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah's atonement-cow in the Gemara, which was not his but his neighbor's, and since he did not protest, it was called by his name). (b) A person must also confess for what he sinned in previous incarnations — and who knows what he did; therefore we say 'we have sinned, we and our fathers,' meaning the previous incarnations are called 'fathers' to this body. (c) A person is judged according to his level, and for the righteous the standard of judgment is exacting to a hairsbreadth (as with Reuben, the sons of Eli, the sons of Samuel, and the sin of Bat-Sheva that was written of David even though she was divorced and had immersed). (d) There are transgressions that a person 'treads underfoot' and considers minor in his own eyes, but which are in truth severe — as our Sages said: one who shames his fellow's face is as though he shed blood; one who becomes angry is as though he worshipped idols; and one who is arrogant is as though he worshipped idols. For all these reasons, one should say all the details of the confession.
takeaways: One says all the details of the confession even for things he did not do — since all Israel are guarantors for one another, and one who did not protest [a wrong] is counted as though he had done it.
Also because of sins from previous incarnations ('our fathers'), because a person is judged according to his own level, and because of seemingly minor transgressions that are in fact severe.

paragraphs: Qodem havvidduy yomar abal chatanu avinu pashanu anachnu vaabotenu veanshe betenu ukemo shekkatub besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l, veken tzarik lehosip bachamishsha otiyyot mntzp"k sheyyomar kazabnu kaasnu maradnu marinu debareka naatznu naapnu pashanu pagamnu tzararnu tzaarnu ab vaem, veken hu besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l:

clarification.explanation: Before the confession itself one should say, 'But we have sinned, we have transgressed, we have committed iniquity — we, our fathers, and the members of our household,' as brought in the siddur of the Rashash. One should also add a further confession text corresponding to the five final-form letters (MaNTzPaKh), containing expressions such as 'we have lied, we have become angry, we have rebelled, we have defied Your words, we have blasphemed, we have committed adultery, we have transgressed, we have caused blemish, we have oppressed, we have grieved father and mother' — and so it is in the siddur of the Rashash.
takeaways: Before the confession one says an opening formula ('But we have sinned'), and adds a further confession built on the letters MaNTzPaKh, as brought in the siddur of the Rashash.

paragraphs: Yakkeh beet havvidduy beyad yamin kapup keegrop al halleb shehu omed betzad semol hakkaot benachat, veal kol teba min havvidduy hakkaa vekannizkar beshaar hakkavvanot ukebar yadua dimqom halleb hu tachat haddad bearba o chamesh etzbaot nimshak letzad panim, vekol adam yihyeh nizhar lehakkot sham al halleb velo keotam hammakkim lemala min haddad o al haddad atzmo deen zeh meqom halleb vehattaam demakkeh al halleb lepi happeshat lehorot dehalleb garam lo kol ellu haavonot, ak beemet en iqqar hattaam ella yesh lazeh taam nistar kepi hassod kamporash bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar hakkavvanot sheoseh haadam behakkaa zo al halleb tiqqun gadol:

clarification.explanation: At the time of saying the confession one should strike with the right hand, curled like a fist, upon the heart which is on the left side — gentle strikes, one strike for every word of the confession. The location of the heart is beneath the chest, about four to five fingers' breadth inward, and one must be careful to strike exactly there and not above the chest or on the chest itself, for that is not the location of the heart. The simple reason is that the heart caused all these sins; but the true reason is esoteric, as explained in the words of the Ari, of blessed memory, that the striking upon the heart effects a great rectification.
takeaways: During the confession one strikes gently with the right hand upon the heart (beneath the chest, not above it or on it directly), one strike for each word — by virtue of a deep esoteric rectification beyond the simple reason.

paragraphs: Achar havvidduy tekep yomar veyaabor vy"g middot, vetzarik leomeram bekavvanot halleb ubenachat ubematun, umatzati katub sheyyimneh y"g middot shello veyaabru beetzbeotayv kederek shemona y" sammane haqqetoret vehu minhag yapeh venakon, veken ani noheg sheyyesh bazeh toelet gadol lemachshaba vekavvana, vegam hamminyan moreh al maala vachashibut haddebarim, veyesh medaqdeqim kesheomerim et hy"g middot letzayyer otiyyot shellahem kiriyyato otam ketubim lepanayv besiddur, achat achat kesidran al daat mah shekkatab haggaon mh"r chayyim molezin za"l bitpillat haamida vehu minhag yapeh, ak baavonotenu harabbim hashlicha tzibbur vehatztzibbur memaharin harbeh biqriatam vehannoheg kak tzarik sheyyishheh harbeh baamiratam, al ken yaaseh mah sheepshar lo laasot: vekatabti besipri haqqatan mqbtzyl im omer adam y"g middot im hatztzibbur vehem memaharim ligmor otam vehu odennu bemachatzitam let lan bah, vahare zeh chashib qoream im hatztzibbur, kevan shehitchil bahem im hatztzibbur:

clarification.explanation: Immediately after the confession one says 'Vaya'avor' and the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy, and one should say them with intention of the heart, calmly and unhurriedly. Some are accustomed to count the Thirteen Attributes on their fingers, in the manner of counting the eleven spice-ingredients of the incense — a fine and proper custom, both for the benefit of concentration and intention, and because the counting itself expresses the importance of the matter. Some are even more meticulous and mentally visualize the letters of the Attributes as though they see them written before them in the siddur, one by one in order. It is regrettable that the prayer leader and the congregation rush greatly through their recitation, and one who is able should linger longer over them. If a person says the Thirteen Attributes together with the congregation, and the congregation rushes to finish while he is still in the middle, there is nothing wrong with this — he is still considered to have said them with the congregation, since he began together with them.
takeaways: One should say the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy calmly, with intention and without haste — not rushed as most of the congregation tends to do; a fine custom is to count them on one's fingers.
One who began reciting them together with the congregation is considered to have said them with the congregation, even if the congregation finishes before him.

paragraphs: Achar havvidduy vaamirat y"g middot tekep umiyyad yaaseh nepilat appayim ki shelosha elleh tzerikim lihyot semukim zeh lazeh, yaan "y amirat havvidduy hamqatreg loqeach chelqo beet havvidduy veholek lo uneparesh mimmeqom haqqedushsha, veaz naasim b' mine zivvugim lemala bishne bechinot haechad beet amirat y"g middot vehashsheni beet nepilat appayim, vezar lo yiqrab el meqom hammiqdash letamme et mishkan Adonai chas veshalom, vekannizkar beshaar hakkavvanot, laken gam besheni vachamishi en lehapsiq ben vidduy linpilat appayim battachanunim hannosapim bayyamim hahem, ella yomru nepilat appayim tekep veaach"k veomedim veomerim otam hattachanunim min el melek veku' ad hassop, upoh irenu bagdad haya minhagam mizzeman qadmon lomar besheni vachamishi kol hattachanunim hannosapim qodem nepilat appayim, utehillot lael bittalnu minhag zeh vehinhagnu lomar nepilat appayim qodem, kemo shekkatab rabbenu haari"y za"l.

clarification.explanation: After the confession and the Thirteen Attributes one must perform Nefilat Apayim immediately, because these three parts must be adjacent to one another. The reason: through the recitation of the confession, the Accuser (the Satan) takes his portion and withdraws from the place of holiness, and then two kinds of spiritual 'unions' are effected above — one at the time of saying the Thirteen Attributes, and the second at the time of Nefilat Apayim — and the 'stranger' (the husk/kelipah) cannot approach to defile the place of holiness. Therefore, even on Mondays and Thursdays, when additional supplications are added, one should not interrupt between the confession and Nefilat Apayim; rather one says Nefilat Apayim immediately, and only afterward stands and says the additional supplications ('E-l Melekh' etc.). In Baghdad the custom from ancient times was to say all the additional supplications on Mondays and Thursdays before Nefilat Apayim, but the Ben Ish Chai abolished this custom and instituted saying Nefilat Apayim first, as the Ari, of blessed memory, wrote.
takeaways: The confession, the Thirteen Attributes, and Nefilat Apayim must be said in one uninterrupted sequence, even on Mondays and Thursdays with their additional supplications.
The Ben Ish Chai changed the old local custom of Baghdad so that Nefilat Apayim is said immediately after the Attributes, before the additional supplications.

paragraphs: Hayyamim sheen omerim bahem vidduy vy"g middot unepilat appayim bevadday hazzivvugim naasim lemala ak naasim mealehem bizkut qedushshat hayyamim hahem, kak margela bepummayhu derabbanan hamqubbalim za"l, veshamati omerim shemminhag hachasidim lekavven kol zeh bemachshaba bilbad, ki ken darkan lekavven bemachshaba kol mitzva shennidchin mechamat shabbat kegon teqiat shopar unetilat lulab, veim tomar hayyamim shehem chol gamur shello ameru bahem vidduy unepilat appayim mechamat dehaya chatan o mila bebet hakkeneset ek yihyu naasim shelemot hazzivvugim lemala bitpillat hatztzibbur shehitpallelu beotah bet hakkeneset, hatteshuba lazeh ditpillat otam hatztzibbur nishlemet mittepillat tzibbur achar sheasu vidduy unepilat appayim, yaan ki lebassop niklalim kol hattepillot shel kol haqqehillot zeh im zeh veolim yachad, vbsh"q mqbtzyl asiti chizzuq letaam zeh mimmah shekkatab mh"r chayyim veyittol za"l beshaar hakkavvanot bidrush hasseper tora, vezeh leshono zeman harbeh hitpallel mori za"l bebeto baasara velo chashash sheyyihyeh sham seper tora liqrot bo ben bechol ben beshabbat ad kan leshono, veek tihyeh tepillato shel rabbenu ner yisrael chasera chas veshalom min hearot sod petichat hahekol veseper tora uqeriat seper tora, ella mukrach lomar shessamak bazeh al shear qehillot shemmotziin seper tora beotam hayyamim, demah sheosin bishar qehillot yoil gam liqhilla shello ki hakkol niklal yachad, veal derek zeh ani omer dehammitpallel im hatztzibbur veheerik bitpillato velo shama hachazara, sheggam tepillato tihyeh shelema besod hachazara, meachar shenniklelet im tepillat otam hatztzibbur veha yapeh mehak, meachar shebbeemet hu mitpallel immahem yachad:

Veda ki bsh"q mqbtzyl hebeti dibre harab emet leyaaqob bispat emet dap q"b ammud d' bashsheela shennishal harab hechasid zemirat haaretz al yamim sheen bahem nepilat appayim mikkoach minhag kemo yamim achar pesach veachar sukkot veken yeme mila vechatan vekayyotze, dimniat nepilat appayim bahem lo nizkar bedibre chaza"l, vekatab hayyare et debar Adonai vehabba besod Adonai tzarik sheyyomar veyaabor unepilat appayim beno leben atzmo veku' ayyen sham, vaana abda piqpaqti bidbarayv, vegam mah shehokicha min rosh chodesh piqpaqti alayv bazeh vegam al sebarat harab emet leyaaqob shechiddesh meatzmo lekavven bebirkat sim shalom piqpaqti, veraq al mah shekkatab lekavven bemachshaba hodeti vetabo alayv beraka, vekatab li yedidenu harab haggaon hechasid mhr" minni nr"v, shemmatza mippi harab hechasid hyr" za"l, shekkatab vezeh leshono minhag qadum bebet el ykb"tz lekavven kol hakkavvanot balleb ben hachazara leqaddish ad kan:

clarification.explanation:
On days when confession, the Thirteen Attributes, and Nefilat Apayim are not said, the [spiritual] unions above still occur, but they occur by themselves, by virtue of the holiness of those days (as the Kabbalists say). And the Ben Ish Chai heard that the custom of the pious is to have this in mind through thought alone — just as it is their way to mentally intend every commandment that is deferred because of Shabbat, such as blowing the shofar or taking the lulav.
And if you should ask: on a plain weekday when confession and Nefilat Apayim were not said because there was a groom or a circumcision in the synagogue — how are the unions above completed from that congregation's prayer? The answer: that congregation's prayer is completed from the prayer of another congregation that did say confession and Nefilat Apayim, since ultimately all the congregations' prayers are joined together and rise as one. He also brought a proof from the words of Rabbi Chaim Vital, of blessed memory (Sha'ar HaKavanot), that the Ari prayed for a long time at his home with a quorum of ten without a Torah scroll — and one must therefore say he relied on the other congregations that were bringing out a Torah scroll, since what is done in them benefits his congregation too, as everything is joined together. In the same way, the Ben Ish Chai says that one who prays with the congregation but prolongs his prayer and misses the [leader's] repetition — his prayer is nevertheless complete by virtue of the secret of the repetition, since it is joined with that congregation's prayer.
He further brings a dispute: some wrote (Rav Emet LeYa'akov) that one who is God-fearing should say Vaya'avor and Nefilat Apayim privately on these days; the Ben Ish Chai had reservations about this, and agreed only with the suggestion to have it in mind through thought. And Rabbi Eliyahu Mani, may his Rock preserve him, wrote to him that an ancient custom in Beit El was to have all the intentions in mind, in the heart, between the repetition and the Kaddish.
takeaways: On days without confession/Nefilat Apayim, the [spiritual] unions occur by themselves through the holiness of the day; the custom of the pious is to have this in mind through thought alone.

A weekday when these were omitted due to a groom or circumcision is completed through the prayer of another congregation, since all prayers are joined and rise together (as with one who missed the repetition).
There is a dispute as to whether one should say 'Vaya'avor' and Nefilat Apayim privately; the main point is to have it in mind through thought, in the heart.

paragraphs: Tzarik lehitvaddot meummad, veken tachanunim hannosapim besheni vachamishi hakkol meummad, velo yismok al dabar sheim yinnatel yippol ella im ken hu zaqen o choleh az muttar lismok al ezeh dabar, veim raa hatztzibbur mitvaddin "p shehu hitvadda yitvaddeh immahem, vekatab beshalme tzibbur sheen haolam nohagin ken veyesh lahem al mah sheyyismoku ayyen sham, venireh li "p shennahagu ken nakon shekkol haroeh tzibbur mitvaddin yomar chatanu avinu pashanu shehu vidduy kelali veqatzar, veen lomar vidduy bemotzae shabbat ad achar chatzot layla, vekatab bechesed laalapim epshar dehu haddin lemotzae rosh chodesh umotzae chanukka upurim vekaddomeh, desheb veal taaseh adip:

clarification.explanation: One must confess while standing, and likewise the additional supplications on Mondays and Thursdays — all while standing; and one should not lean on anything that would fall if removed, unless he is elderly or ill, in which case he is permitted to lean. And if he sees the congregation confessing — even though he has already confessed — he should confess together with them. And Shalmei Tzibbur writes that people do not customarily act this way and have grounds to rely upon; nevertheless, it seems to the Ben Ish Chai that it is proper that anyone who sees a congregation confessing should say at least 'We have sinned, we have committed iniquity, we have transgressed' — a general and brief confession. And one does not say the confession on Motza'ei Shabbat until after midnight; and the Chesed LaAlafim writes that perhaps the same applies to the conclusion of Rosh Chodesh, Chanukah, and Purim, and the like — since it is better to refrain [from an act in doubt].
takeaways: One confesses standing (and likewise the Monday/Thursday supplications), and does not lean unless elderly or ill.
One who sees a congregation confessing should join them, saying at least 'We have sinned, we have committed iniquity, we have transgressed.'
There is no confession on Motza'ei Shabbat until after midnight (and possibly the same at the conclusion of Rosh Chodesh/Chanukah/Purim).

paragraphs: Asur lehazkir y"g middot ballayla, velaken otam hammitpallelim mincha besop hayyom im sheqiat hachamma, im beet shehiggiu levidduy abar qeriat hmgr"b shehu sop y"b shaot mammash, lo yomru y"g middot ella yomru vidduy lebaddo:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to mention the Thirteen Attributes at night. Therefore, those who pray the Minchah service at the end of the day, near sunset — if, by the time they reached the confession, the time of the 'Maghrib' [the Muslim call to the evening prayer, marking the end of the twelve seasonal daytime hours] had already passed — should not say the Thirteen Attributes, but only the confession alone.
takeaways: The Thirteen Attributes may not be said at night; one who prays Minchah too close to sundown, past the end of the day, says only the confession without the Thirteen Attributes.

paragraphs: En hayyachid omer y"g middot ki hem dabar shebbiqdushsha shetztzarik asara, vehammitpallel beyachid kesheyyomar y"g middot achar havvidduy yomar otam bitamim keqore battora, veayyen baacharonim za"l vaani noheg besheni vachamishi beyachid lomar y"g middot deachar havvidduy bitamim, ella omer kemo shehodaetta leanav miqqodem vetu la middi, umin "veken katub betorateka veku'" ad sop y"g middot ani roeh besiddur umekavven otam bemachshaba bilbad, kak hayiti noheg mikkamma shanim kesheani mitpallel beyachid besheni vachamishi, mihu aach"k raiti beseper keter malkut ketibat yad shekkatab hayyachid lo yomar y"g middot bilshon tora ella rashshay leomeram bilshon targum, sheyyomar kak vaeebor Adonai shekkinteh al appohi, veqara Adonai Adonai elaha rachamana vechannana, marchiq raggaz, umasge lemebad tibbun uqeshot, natar tibo lealpe darin, shabeq leivvuyan velimrod ulechobin, selach lidtayyebin leorayeteh ad kan hattargum, veacharayv yomar baqqasha zo ana Adonai el chay taspiq lanu shepa or uberaka chen vachesed verachamim veometz, na Adonai el podeh, ittarnu sammechenu ad kan ubaqqasha zo kol debarim shebbah hemma metzorapim min otiyyot y"g middot shehem Adonai Adonai el rachum vechannun veku' ad kan dibre seper keter malkut hannizkar, vaani noheg bekak achar hammachashaba sheani mechashsheb by"g middot:

clarification.explanation: An individual is not permitted to say the Thirteen Attributes in the ordinary manner, because they are considered a 'matter of sanctity' requiring a quorum of ten. Therefore, one who prays alone, upon reaching the Thirteen Attributes after the confession, should say them with the Torah cantillation notes, as one reading from the Torah (this being a way to circumvent the problem of reciting them as an ordinary sacred matter). The Ben Ish Chai relates that he himself is accustomed, when praying alone on Mondays and Thursdays, to say only the beginning of 'Vaya'avor' with cantillation, up to 'as You made known to the humble one of old,' while from 'and thus it is written in Your Torah' to the end of the Thirteen Attributes he merely looks at the siddur and has it in mind through thought alone — so he was accustomed for many years. Later he found written in the manuscript book Keter Malkhut that an individual should not say the Thirteen Attributes in the language of the Torah at all, but is permitted to say them in Aramaic translation; and after the translation he should add a special petition whose every word is constructed from the letters of the Thirteen Attributes. The Ben Ish Chai notes that he is accustomed to do so, combined with the thought-intention he has in mind for the Thirteen Attributes.
takeaways: An individual does not say the Thirteen Attributes in the ordinary manner, since they are a matter of sanctity requiring a quorum; one may say them with Torah cantillation (as though reading from the Torah), or alternatively in Aramaic translation.

paragraphs: Beshaa sheomer veyaabor yishcheh meat, veyizqop beshem, kesheomer Adonai Adonai el rachum vechannun, vetob sheyyarim qolo ubitnay shello yaligu habberiyyot, kak katab bechesed laalapim veshaalti lididenu harab haggaon mhr" manni nr"v lehodieni minhag qehal chasidim bebet el ykb"tz beir haqqodesh tibbaneh vetikkonen vekatab li: hamminhag pashut sheshshochin meat betebat vayyaabru Adonai al panayv ubetebat vayyiqra magbihin rosham, vegam betebat Adonai Adonai shochin meat, veayyen shiyyure beraka siman ql"ch veshalme tzibbur dap qm"t ammud ' ukepi hassod lo nimtza taam lazeh behedya amenam hallomed hakkavvanot bediqduq verotzeh laasot semek lamminhag yukal benaqel, vaani qibbalti shebbetebat Adonai Adonai lehagbihha raglayv velo matzati lazeh galuy besipre happoseqim veap al pi ken ani noheg ken, sheim lo yoil lo yazziq ad kan debarayv nr"v:

clarification.explanation: At the time one says 'Vaya'avor' he should bow slightly, and stand upright at the [divine] Name — when he says 'The Lord, the Lord, God, merciful and gracious.' It is good to raise one's voice, provided that people will not mock him for it (Chesed LaAlafim). And the Ben Ish Chai asked Rabbi Eliyahu Mani, may his Rock preserve him, about the custom of the congregation of the pious in Beit El: the plain custom is to bow slightly at the words 'and the Lord passed by before him,' and at the word 'and proclaimed' to raise the head, and likewise to bow slightly at the words 'The Lord, The Lord.' And he wrote that according to the esoteric teaching no explicit reason is found for this, though one who has studied the intentions in detail can easily find support for it; and he added that he received the tradition to raise his feet at the words 'The Lord, The Lord,' though he did not find this stated explicitly in the works of the halachic authorities — and nevertheless he is accustomed to do so, since 'if it does not help, it will not harm.'
takeaways: At 'Vaya'avor' one bows slightly, and stands upright at the divine Name, 'The Lord, The Lord, God, merciful and gracious'; it is good to raise one's voice if this will not draw mockery.
The custom of Beit El: bowing at 'Vaya'avor... [the Lord] passed by,' and at 'The Lord, The Lord,' and raising the head at 'and proclaimed' (and some raise their feet at 'The Lord, The Lord').

paragraphs: Yizzaher lehatim hepseq asher ben Adonai | Adonai, ki sodo gadol umi sheeno matim oto anesho gadol vekannizkar bechesed laalapim ayyen sham, veayyen beshaar hakkavvanot. gam ayyen beseper hallequtim hannidpas beir haqqodesh yerushalayim tibbaneh vetikkonen bimhera beyimmanu beparashat ki tissa mah sheheerik besod hannizkar vesod hepseq ayyen sham:

clarification.explanation: One should be careful to give a slight pause between the first word 'the Lord' and the second word 'the Lord' in the verse 'The Lord, the Lord, God, merciful and gracious,' because there is a great secret in this, and one who does not make this distinction incurs a great punishment, as written in the Chesed LaAlafim and explained also in Sha'ar HaKavanot.
takeaways: One should give a slight pause between the two utterances of 'the Lord' in the verse of the Thirteen Attributes, on account of a great secret contained in that separation.

paragraphs: Im hatztzibbur betzaar al kol min tzara shello tabo az im yeera mila beotam hayyamim tob sheyyomru hatztzibbur y"g middot shel rachamim bekavvana ben mila lipria, vehu dabar mesuggal kannizkar bechesed lealpayim:

clarification.explanation: If the congregation is in some kind of distress, may no trouble come, and on those days a circumcision takes place, it is good that the congregation say the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy with intention between the circumcision and the peri'ah — this is an especially efficacious matter, as written in the Chesed LaAlafim.
takeaways: In a time of communal distress, when there is a circumcision, it is recommended to say the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy with intention between the circumcision and the peri'ah — a special remedy for [invoking divine] mercy.

paragraphs: Achar y"g middot yomru meummad rachum vechannun chatanu lepaneka rachem alenu vehoshienu, veaach"k mizmor ledavid eleka Adonai napshi essa meyushshab, veniqra mizmor zeh nepilat appayim deiqqaro nitqan leamero binpilat appayim sheyyappil panayv al zeroo hassemali vetzarik lehizzaher shello yasim panayv tok yado hassemalit deyesh sakkana chas veshalom, ella yasim panayv al zeroo hassemalit, vikasseh panayv betallit vetzarik lehizzaher binpilat appayim ben beshacharit ben bemincha, vekatub beseper hakkavvanot kavvanot amuqqot binpilat appayim shemmoser atzmo lemita shemmekavven lehorid napsho ad meqom hammita shehem haqqelippot ulekavven sheyyotzi mishsham otam habberurim veku' veku', vehazzokeh laasot nepilat appayim ketiqnah sekaro gadol veoyebayv nopelim lepanayv, ak baavonotenu harabbim en ittanu yodea bedabar zeh veen banu koach lekak: vehinneh poh ayarenu bgd"d y" en nohagim lehasim penehem al zeroam kelal hen adam gadol hen qatan hen chakam hen pashut, vegam en shum echad mekavven limsor napsho al qiddush hashshem velo kavvana acheret ella raq omerim hammizmor hazzeh belachash umah sheyyereim umepachadim bazeh harbeh hu ki chosheshim el dibre zohar haqqadosh sheamar (bammidbar q"b) vay leh lemaen deamar eleka Adonai napshi essa velav kol millohi veku' ella belibba rachiqa vela biruta veku', veal da bae bar nash leiddabqa napsheh vereoteha bemiarya, vela yati legabbeh bemille kidyabo, diktib (tehillim q, z) dober sheqarim lo yikkon leneged enay veku' ayyen sham, mihu gam leminhag irenu tzarik haadam lehizzaher lomar mizmor zeh benachat ubilbabo yabin mah shemmotzi bispatayv, vekatabti lididenu harab haggaon hechasid mhr" minni nr"v lehodieni minhag qehal chasidim bebet el ykb"tz birushalayim t"v im mannichim penehem al zeroam, vekatab li en mannichim penehem al zeroam veen meshannim mishshear hattepilla, veyesh notenim taam lepi dekavvanot nepilat appayim arukkot velo epshar al peh umukrachim lehabbit bassiddur shebbeyadam, veyesh omerim dehattayat harosh al hazzeroa hi atzmah mora al yeridat hannepesh bimqom haddin, ulekavven lehorid napsho leimqe haqqelippot kede lebarer, umeachar daanachenu mitpachadim lehorid hannepesh limqom haqqelippa, im ken lamma lanu lehattot al tzad semol lehorot al dabar zeh shel hayyerida ad kan debarayv nr"v, ubevadday detob shekkol adam yimna atzmo shello yasim panayv al zeroo velo yaaseh shum shinnuy kelal:

clarification.explanation: After the Thirteen Attributes one says while standing, 'Merciful and gracious One, we have sinned before You; have mercy on us and save us,' and afterward, sitting, the psalm 'To You, O Lord, I lift up my soul.' This psalm is called Nefilat Apayim, because it was originally instituted to be said while tilting the face upon the left arm — but one must be careful not to place the face literally inside the left hand (which involves danger), but rather upon the arm. One should cover the face with the tallit, and observe this both in Shacharit and Minchah. Sha'ar HaKavanot explains that Nefilat Apayim contains a profound intention of self-sacrifice — bringing the soul down to the place of the husks and extracting sparks of holiness from there — and one who merits doing this properly has a great reward, with his enemies falling before him. But because of our many sins we do not know how to do this, so in Baghdad — young and old, scholar and simple person alike — no one places his face on his arm at all, nor has any intention of self-sacrifice; rather, they only say the psalm in a whisper, out of fear stemming from the words of the holy Zohar, which warned that saying 'To You, O Lord, I lift up my soul' without true intention ('with a distant heart and without will') may be considered as 'speaking lies.' Nevertheless, one must be careful to say the psalm calmly and understand in the heart what is uttered by the lips. Also in Beit El, Jerusalem, they do not place the face on the arm, for the reason that the intentions are too lengthy to remember by heart, and also because if one is afraid to intentionally bring the soul down to the place of the husks, there is no point in tilting the head to symbolize that very descent. Therefore it is fitting that every person refrain from placing the face upon the arm and make no change in the text.
takeaways: In practice: one must not place the face literally inside the hand (danger), but at most upon the arm — and in Baghdad and Jerusalem the custom today is not to do so at all, but rather to say the psalm quietly while sitting.

The profound intentions of Nefilat Apayim (self-sacrifice, descending to extract sparks) are reserved for one who knows how to properly intend them; one who does not know should say the psalm calmly and with understanding.

paragraphs: Yesh nohagim shello laasot nepilat appayim ella bemaqom sheyyesh aron veseper tora, o beezrat bet hakkeneset, veen haemet ken ella kepi hassod tzarik laasot nepilat appayim bekol maqom, vaapillu beyachid, veen laasot nepilat appayim ballayla, vekol sheyyesh lahem sapeq dehaynu ben hashshemashot lo yaasu nepilat appayim desheb veal taaseh adip, veachar mizmor ledavid eleka Adonai napshi essa omerim abinu malkenu veku' vehi tepilla utechinna noraa:

clarification.explanation: Some are accustomed not to perform Nefilat Apayim except in a place that has a Holy Ark and a Torah scroll, or in the main sanctuary — but this is an error. According to the esoteric teaching, one should perform Nefilat Apayim in any place, even when praying alone. One should not perform Nefilat Apayim at night, and likewise in any case of doubt (such as twilight), one should not perform it, on the principle that it is better to refrain. After the psalm 'To You, O Lord, I lift up my soul,' one says 'Avinu Malkeinu,' and so forth — an awesome prayer and supplication.
takeaways: Nefilat Apayim may be performed anywhere, even alone, and not only in a place with a Holy Ark; but it should not be performed at night or at a time of doubt.

paragraphs: Kesheomer ashre utehilla ledavid yekavven bammizmor hazzeh meod, ubiprat bepasuq poteach et yadeka, umah shekkatab rabbotenu za"l (berakot d:): haomer "tehilla ledavid" shelosh peamim bekol yom mubtach lo shehu ben olam habba, haynu im amaro bekavvanat halleb karauy, az yagen alayv lihyot ben olam habba, ubeamero uba letziyyon goel uleshabe pesha, yekavven rashe tebot goel velishbi pesha hu gup, verashe tebot beyaaqob neum Adonai vaani bny"v, vikavven bazeh ki banayv sheyyeredu lachitzonim "y aon shikbat zera lebattala, hinneh atta al yede teshubato yachzeru leotzar hanneshamot hanniqra beshem gup, veyabo haggoel vekannizkar bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l:

clarification.explanation: When saying 'Ashrei' and 'Tehillah LeDavid' one should have great intention, especially in the verse 'You open Your hand.' What our Sages said — that one who says 'Tehillah LeDavid' three times a day is assured to be a son of the World to Come — means specifically when it is said with true intention of the heart; then it protects him to be a son of the World to Come. When saying 'U'va LeTziyon go'el ulshavei fesha beYa'akov' [And a redeemer shall come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from transgression], one should intend that the initial letters of 'go'el ulshavei fesha' spell 'guf' (body), and the initial letters of 'beYa'akov ne'um Hashem' [and 'va'ani' - and I] spell 'banav' (his children) — and intend that a person's 'children,' who descended to the husks ('external ones') through the sin of wasted seed, now return, through his repentance, to the 'treasury of souls' called 'body,' and the redeemer will come.
takeaways: The assurance of being 'a son of the World to Come' for one who says 'Tehillah LeDavid' three times daily is conditional on true intention of the heart in saying it.
In 'U'va LeTziyon' one should intend, by the secret of the initial letters, that even lost sparks (from the sin of wasted seed) can return to rectification through repentance.

paragraphs: Qedushshat uba letziyyon hi hanniqret qedushsha desidra, mippene ki haacharonim sidderu otah dugmat qedushsha daamida kannizkar beshibbole halleqet shehebio b"bet yosep", depaam achat gazeru haoyebam al yisrael shello yomru qedushsha battepilla, vehayu mannichim orebim umamtinim ad sheyyigmeru haamida im hachazara veholekim, lekak hitqinu lomar seder qedushsha kan, veachar shebbittelum miqqedushshat haamida uqedushshat yotzer al ken tiqqenu lomar qedushsha zo bilshon haqqodesh uleshon targum keneged shette qedushshot, ulekak qorin otah qedushsha desidra shennisdera keneged shette qedushshot hannizkarot, veap al gab debatela haggezera lo bittelu qedushsha zo aach"k, mippene shebbeemet yesh bah taam al pi hassod, umah shello tiqqenu otah anshe keneset haggedola meiqqara mippene sheadayin lo haya hazzeman harauy umetuqqan letiqqun zeh, vekaasher higgia hazzeman harauy lekak sibbeb hqb"h sibba hannizkeret shebbaaburah tiqqenu qedushsha zo kan, velaken lo bitteluha aach"k "p shebbatela hasibba, mechamat ki rau chaza"l berucha qadesham shebbeemet rauy lihyot qedushsha kan "p hassod, od yesh taam acher mah shenniqret qedushsha desidra mippene shehi taqqana chadasha shello nitqena meanshe keneset haggedola im qedushshat yotzer uqedushshat haamida, venitqena kan mippene ki kan hi sod yeridat hammalkut bibria behekal qadeshe qodashim, velaken omerim atta qadosh ubaruk veyimlok leolam vaed, kede lehamshik shepa haqqedushsha, desidra perush shennitqena "p seder haolamot veomerim otah kesidran shel olamot, venahagu lomar hattargum belachash kemo shekkatub beshulchan aruk, v"g dekatab morenu harab chayyim veyittol za"l derabbenu haari"y za"l haya omeram beqol ram, veod shamati shemminhag hachasidim bebet el ykb"tz deen medaqdeqim bazeh ella lipamim belachash lipamim beqol ram, hinneh poh bgd"d nohagim ledaqdeq bazeh lomar belachash davqa deim lo yoil lo yazziq:

clarification.explanation: The Kedushah of 'U'va LeTziyon' is called 'Kedushah DeSidra,' since the later authorities arranged it as a parallel to the Kedushah of the Amidah. The background: once the enemies of Israel decreed that Kedushah must not be said in prayer, and they would lie in ambush, waiting for the congregation to finish the repetition (including the Kedushah), and then leave. Therefore an additional order of Kedushah was instituted here — after the decree against the Kedushah of the Amidah and of Yotzer had been rescinded — to be said both in the holy tongue and in Aramaic translation, corresponding to the two Kedushot that had been forbidden and later restored. That is why it is called 'Kedushah DeSidra' — arranged corresponding to two Kedushot. Although the decree was later annulled, this Kedushah was not subsequently annulled, since it has a deep reason according to the esoteric teaching; and the reason the Men of the Great Assembly did not institute it from the start is that the proper time for this institution had not yet arrived, and when the time came, the Holy One, blessed be He, brought about the aforementioned episode of the decree so that this Kedushah would be instituted here — and therefore it was not later annulled even though the original cause was annulled, because our Sages saw with their holy spirit that it is truly fitting for there to be a Kedushah here, according to the esoteric teaching. Another reason for its name: it is a new institution that was not instituted together with the Kedushah of Yotzer and of the Amidah by the Men of the Great Assembly, but instituted here because this place expresses, in secret, the descent of Malkhut into the World of Creation, in the Sanctuary of the Holy of Holies — therefore here we say 'Kadosh,' 'Baruch,' and 'Yimlokh le'olam va'ed,' in order to draw down the flow of holiness, and it is called 'DeSidra' also because it was instituted according to the order of the worlds. It is customary to say the Aramaic translation in this Kedushah in a whisper, as fixed in the Shulchan Aruch, although there is testimony that the Ari said it aloud, and the pious of Beit El are not exacting about this; in Baghdad the custom is to be exacting and say the translation specifically in a whisper.
takeaways: The Kedushah of 'U'va LeTziyon' ('Kedushah DeSidra') was instituted as a substitute during the period when the Kedushah of prayer was forbidden, but it remained even after the ban was lifted, for a deep esoteric reason.
It is customary to say the Aramaic translation in this Kedushah in a whisper (the Baghdad custom), although there is testimony of other customs.

paragraphs: Qodem mizmore hayyamim yomar hayyom yom echad beshabbat, im hu yom rishon beshabbat, veken hu haddin beyom sheni yomar hayyom yom sheni beshabbat, vehu haddin leyom shelishi, ushear yamim, veraq beyom shishshi yosip ot he" veyomar hayyom yom hashshishshi behe" yetera, veken beyom rishon yedaqdeq lomar yom echad beshabbat qodesh, vikavven beminyan zeh bekol yom leqayyem mitzvat zakor et yom hashshabbat (shemot k, ch), deameru rabbotenu za"l besipre (sham) shehu mitzvat aseh min hattora limnot bo yeme hashshabua lomar echad beshabbat sheni beshabbat veku' veken katab haramba"n za"l, vehainyan hu lehorot dime hachol teluyim veniqsharim beshabbat shemmishsham nimsheka lahem hearatam ukemo shekkatab rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar hakkavvanot, ubeyamim sheen omeram bahem vidduy hamminhag pashut deen omerim mizmor yaanka umizmor tepilla ledavid, veken hamminhag gam etzel qehal chasidim beir haqqodesh yerushalayim t"v velo yadanu taam lemizmor tepilla ledavid veomerim dekak hu qabbala meharishonim za"l: veda ki poh ayarenu bgd"d y" haya hamminhag mizzeman qadmon dekol yom taanit tzibbur sheomerim bo mizmor hashshayyak lo, veken bemotzae kippur ubachanukka ubepurim sheyyesh lahem mizmorim hashshayyakim lahem deen omerim bet yaaqob mizmor haqqabua lime hashshabua ella raq omerim mizmor hashshayyak limora bilbad, utehillot lael yitbarek tiqqanti hamminhag bekol batte kenesiyyot shebbeirenu lomar bet yaaqob umizmor hashshayyak leoto hayyom shel yeme hashshabua, veaach"k omerim mizmor hashshayyak leoto meora, vetiqqanti gam ken sheyyomru beoto hayyom qodem mizmor shel yeme hashshabua hayyom yom veku' shir shehayu omerim halleviyyim kemo sheomerim bishar hayyamim, hen beyamim shel taanit tzibbur hen bemotzae kippur, veraq bachanukka tiqqanti shello yomru shir shehayu halleviyyim omerim al haddukan ella raq yomru hayyom yom peloni beshabbat qodesh, veomerim mizmor hashshabua veacharayv mizmor shel chanukka, ki shamati shekken hamminhag beir haqqodesh tvb"b veal yom rosh chodesh lo darashti betzibbur lehedya sheyyomru gam ken bet yaaqob umizmor yom hashshabua, veraq ani omer lichidim hashshoalim oti sheyyomru bet yaaqob umizmor hashshabua qodem musap, veyomru gam ken hayyom yom peloni beshabbat qodesh, veachar musap yomru bareki napshi kamminhag haqqadum, veyesh qetzat batte kenesiyyot shellamedu hachazzanim laasot ken betzibbur sham, umah shello darashti al rosh chodesh betzibbur uqebatim lechoq bekol batte kenesiyyot yesh li taam bazeh, al ken kol qehilla bishar meqomot im yesh lahem minhag kemo minhag haqqadum shehaya poh irenu lebilti yomru bayyamim hannizkarim leel bet yaaqob umizmor yeme hashshabua, shetztzerikin leshannot minhagam velomar bet yaaqob umizmor yeme hashshabua veacharehem mizmor hashshayyak lamora shebbeoto hayyom, umi sheeno oseh ken hare zeh oseh chaseru gadol betiqqun chaza"l shettiqqenu bitpilla:

clarification.explanation: Before the psalms of the day, one says 'Today is the first day toward Shabbat' if it is Sunday, and correspondingly for the rest of the days of the week; only on Friday does one add the letter heh and say 'Today is the sixth day' with an extra heh; and on Sunday one is precise to say 'the first day toward the holy Shabbat.' One should intend, in this daily count, to fulfill the positive Torah commandment of 'Remember the Sabbath day,' since our Sages said this is a positive commandment from the Torah — to count the days of the week and say 'first day toward Shabbat, second day toward Shabbat,' etc. — and so wrote the Ramban, in order to indicate that the weekdays are dependent upon and bound to Shabbat, from which their illumination is drawn. On days when confession is not said, the plain custom is also not to say the psalm 'Ya'ankha' or the psalm 'Tefillah LeDavid,' and so is the custom also among the pious of Jerusalem, though no clear reason is known for the omission of 'Tefillah LeDavid' — it is a received tradition from the early authorities. The Ben Ish Chai relates a further custom he instituted in Baghdad: previously, on public fast days, at the conclusion of Yom Kippur, on Chanukah, and on Purim, they would not say 'Beit Ya'akov' and the ordinary weekly psalm, but only the psalm specific to that day. He instituted in all the synagogues of his city that they should first say 'Beit Ya'akov' and the weekly psalm as usual, and afterward the psalm specific to that occasion — and also say the ordinary 'Today is...' before the weekly psalm. The exception is Chanukah, for which he instituted that they should not say the song the Levites used to say on the platform, but only 'Today is such-and-such day' and the weekly psalm, followed by the Chanukah psalm — as is customary in Jerusalem. Regarding Rosh Chodesh, he did not preach this publicly, but advised individuals who asked him to say 'Beit Ya'akov' and the weekly psalm before Musaf, and 'Today is...,' and after Musaf to say 'Barchi Nafshi' as per the ancient custom. In practice, the Ben Ish Chai ruled that any community elsewhere that follows the old custom [of omitting the weekly psalm] must change its custom and say 'Beit Ya'akov' and the weekly psalm followed by the occasion's psalm; and one who does not do so causes a great deficiency in the institution that our Sages established in the prayer service.
takeaways: Saying 'Today is [day]...' before the daily psalms fulfills the Torah's positive commandment of 'Remember the Sabbath day,' according to our Sages and the Ramban.

Everywhere one must say 'Beit Ya'akov' and the ordinary weekly psalm, followed by the special occasion's psalm (fast day, conclusion of Yom Kippur, Purim); a community that was accustomed to skip the weekly psalm must change its custom, and one who does not do so causes a great deficiency in the Sages' institution.

paragraphs: En kelohenu hu shebach nora veyesh bo kavvana gedola "p hassod, veyomar oto benachat, veacharayv amirat pittum haqqetoret bekavvana gedola, verabbo veatzmo shebacheh, veaach"k omerim qaddish al yisrael veniqra qaddish yatma - shettiqqenu leomero hayyetomim limnuchat nepesh abihem o immam, veyesh bo toelet lenepesh hanniptar lav davqa lehatztzilo middin veonesh ella yoil lo lehaaloto mimmadrega lemadrega, lekak omerim oto bekol yom yartzayt apillu achar kamma shanim mishshenniptar, veken haya noheg rabbenu haari"y za"l leomero bekol shana beyom yartzayt shel abiv. ki immo odenna bachayyim upoh irenu bgd"d nohagim lomar achar qaddish zeh rabbanan bareku et Adonai hamborak, abal beare haqqodesh tvb"b ushear meqomot lo nahagu lomar tebat rabbanan, veod nohagim poh irenu y" lomar rabbanan gam beqaddish deqodem alenu leshebach ditpillat arbit, veken nohagim lomar gam ken rabbanan baaliyyatam leseper tora, velo asinu shinnuy minhag bazeh "p sherob haqqehillot ubiprat beartzot hatztzebi lo nahagu lomar rabbanan, mishshum dela raiti sheyyesh bedabar zeh hepsed upiqpuq kede shennishna hamminhag, laken kol maqom shennahagu bekak yishshaaru beminhagam, ubesipre haqqadosh rab pealim katabti bs"d bitshuba taam laamirat rabbanan bebareku deachar qaddish yatma hu ki bareku deqodem yotzer hu mittaqqanot anshe keneset haggedola shettiqqenu kederek sheomerim bashshamayim ken ukemo shekkatab bammidrash, abal kan lo tiqqenu keneset haggedola lomar bareku ella hachakamim haacharonim tiqqenu oto lekak haomer bareku omer rabbanan bareku veku' kelomar birshut rabbanan ani omer bareku et Adonai hamborak veken hainyan bebareku daaliyyat seper tora shezzeh gam ken lo nitqan meanshe keneset haggedola, veayyen "hashshomer emet" siman y' ot ' yeuyyan sham: veachar aniyyat bareku yaamdu haqqahal veyomru bekavvana gedola alenu leshabbeach vehu shebach elyon venora meod, veyesh bo tzorek gadol litpilla asher hitpallalnu, kede lebattel achizat hachitzonim, ubikria sheanachnu osim beharkanat harosh uqetzat min haggup anachnu moridin or hammaqqip derek yerida bekol haolamot ad haasiyya kullah, vetzarik lomar hashshebach hazzeh kullo meummad, vehizhir rabbenu haari"y za"l shello yachalotz tzitzit utepillin ella ad gemar Adonai echad ushemo echad, vikavven sheppasuq zeh matchil beot v' umesayyem beot d' shehem mispar asara, remez laasara hvyv"t bemilluy hhy"n shehu b"n shenniqraim asara banim sheyyairu belea, haremuza berashe tebot vehaya Adonai lammelek shehu l"v mispar lea veshem hvy"h beemtza remez lahavayot hannizkarim, veim echad eno mitpallel im hatztzibbur veshama hatztzibbur omerim vaanachnu mishtachavim veku' gam hu yishtachaveh immahem, "p sheen kan chiyyub kemo din modim, vekatab bechesed laalapim kesheomer el el lo yoshia yapsiq meat, veaach"k yomar vaanachnu mishtachavim, veim era aniyyat amen kesheomer "shehem mishtachavim lehebel variq" veken kesheomer "umitpallim el el lo yoshia" lo yaaneh sham amen, vehamminhag lomar achar pasuq vehaya Adonai lemelek veku' pasuq vehaya im shamoa tishma. leqol Adonai eloheka veku' ad ki ani Adonai ropeeka:

clarification.explanation: 'Ein KeElokeinu' is an awesome praise with great intention according to the esoteric teaching, and it should be said calmly; afterward, one says 'Pittum HaKetoret' with great intention. Then one says the Kaddish for Israel, called 'Kaddish Yatoma' (the Orphan's Kaddish), which was instituted for orphans to recite for the repose of their father's or mother's soul; its benefit is not only to save from judgment and punishment, but to elevate the soul from level to level — therefore it is said on every Yahrzeit even many years after the passing, and the Ari was accustomed to say it every year on his father's Yahrzeit. In Baghdad the custom is to say after this Kaddish, 'Rabbanan, Barchu et Hashem hamevorach' (with the word 'Rabbanan'), which is not the custom in Jerusalem and elsewhere; likewise in Baghdad they say 'Rabbanan' in the Kaddish before 'Aleinu LeShabe'ach' at the evening service, and when called up to the Torah — because in this Barchu (unlike the ordinary Barchu before Yotzer, instituted by the Men of the Great Assembly), the institution is from later Sages, so one says 'with the permission of our Rabbis, I say Barchu.' After answering Barchu, the congregation rises and says, with great intention, 'Aleinu LeShabe'ach,' which nullifies the grip of the external [powers]; and by the bowing (bending the head and part of the body) one draws down the 'encompassing' light through all the worlds down to the World of Action. One must say this entire praise standing, and should not remove tzitzit or tefillin until completing 'the Lord is One and His Name is One' — this verse begins with vav and ends with dalet, whose sum is ten, alluding to the ten manifestations of the Tetragrammaton in the spelled-out form of the letter heh (called 'Ben'), which illuminate 'Leah' (alluded to in the initial letters of 'VeHayah Hashem LeMelekh,' which also equals thirty-six, the numerical value of 'Leah,' with the Name Havayah in the middle alluding to those manifestations). One who is not praying with the congregation but hears them saying 'Va'anachnu mishtachavim' should also bow with them, though this is not a strict obligation as with 'Modim.' One should pause briefly before 'Va'anachnu mishtachavim' (after 'a god that cannot save'), and should not answer Amen on 'who bow down to vanity and emptiness' or on 'and pray to a god that cannot save.' It is customary to say, after 'VeHayah Hashem LeMelekh,' also the verse 'VeHayah im shamo'a tishma... until 'for I am the Lord your Healer.'
takeaways: In Baghdad they say 'Rabbanan' before the Barchu following the Orphan's Kaddish, before Aleinu LeShabe'ach, and when called to the Torah — since this Barchu was instituted by later Sages, not the Men of the Great Assembly.

'The Lord is One and His Name is One' (beginning with vav, ending with dalet = 10) alludes to the ten manifestations of the Tetragrammaton in the spelling of the letter heh, which illuminate 'Leah'; one should not remove tzitzit and tefillin before completing it.
Precision regarding Amen: one does not answer on 'who bow down to vanity and emptiness' or 'and pray to a god that cannot save.'
